chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hanan, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام.
Concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger" to the end of the verse.
He عليه السلام said: "He is not to be traded with, nor given shelter, nor fed, nor should charity be given to him."

key_terms.يُؤْوَى: he is given shelter or refuge
key_terms.يُبَايَعُ: he is traded with or engaged with in commercial exchange
key_terms.يُحَارِبُونَ: they wage war; in context, they engage in hostile corruption against divine and lawful order

ai.seo_question: What does the verse about waging war against Allah and His Messenger imply in practical legal terms?
ai.summary: This hadith cites the verse regarding those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and explains part of its practical social consequence. Imam Abu Abdillah عليه السلام states that such a person is to be socially boycotted: no trading with him, no sheltering him, no feeding him, and no charity for him.
